cohort: The study included 86 full-term parturients undergoing lower segment caesarean section.
finding: While no significant correlation was found between the fall in cerebral oxygenation and mean blood pressure during spinal anesthesia, NIRS effectively predicted post-spinal hypotension earlier, and timely correction prevented adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, with ephedrine being superior to phenylephrine in improving cerebral oxygenation.
mod_finding: In full-term parturients undergoing lower segment caesarean section, no adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes related to spinal hypotension were observed if the hypotension was promptly corrected.
followup_time: Up to 2 days post-operation for maternal outcomes and 5 minutes post-birth for neonatal outcomes.
